claims.text: Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems can be used to produce a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Compositionally complex or high-entropy alloy systems are resistant to temper embrittlement.
Resistance to temper embrittlement enables a ductile–brittle–ductile transition.
Temperature variation within the proposed transition range acts as the intervention.
The relevant transition occurs within a narrow temperature window.
Alloy composition and microstructure mediate the response to temperature variation.
The predicted response is a ductile–brittle–ductile transition without significant loss of ductility.
Conventional alloys exhibit temper embrittlement and provide the baseline comparison.

contradictions.description: A ductile–brittle–ductile transition necessarily includes an intermediate brittle or reduced-ductility regime, yet the predicted outcome says there is no significant ductility loss and the falsification rule treats a significant ductility decrease as disproof.
Resistance to temper embrittlement could explain retention of ductility, but it does not coherently explain the proposed intervening brittle state.
